biggest_catch: Hourly pay with variable shifts means total Election Day earnings depend on hours assigned — a short shift at $17.50/hr is modest pay.
catches: Election-period only temporary work, not steady employment.
Must be a registered Colorado voter, pass a background check, attend all required trainings.
Hiring runs through party caucus lists first; unaffiliated voters contacted later; not all applicants are contacted for every election.
Provide own meals/beverages and arrange own transportation.

c1.evidence: Official Jefferson County, CO Clerk & Recorder page (jeffco.us/608/Be-an-Election-Worker).

c2.evidence: 'Pay ranges from $17.50 to $18.50 per hour.' Trainings attended with pay. Colorado VSPCs operate 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. on Election Day; assignments vary (ballot processing, VSPC, call center).

c3.evidence: No fee to apply or serve.

c4.evidence: No risk capital; hourly wage for time worked.

eligibility: Registered Colorado voter, 15+; not a candidate/family member of candidate; no fraud/election-offense conviction; background check; oath of office.
notes: Jefferson County, CO (Golden) — rank ~108 by population. Current official page (crawled Sept 2026). 2019 county notice capped shifts at ~8 hrs/day for 2-4 weeks; Election Day VSPC shifts ~12 hrs.
numeric_basis: payout from official Jeffco page ($17.50-$18.50/hr); time: shifts vary by assignment (Election Day ~12 hrs; pre-election assignments up to 8-hr days) plus paid training.
payout_quote: Pay ranges from $17.50 to $18.50 per hour.
payout_value_note: Hourly rate, not flat: $17.50-$18.50/hr; a 12-hr Election Day at $17.50/hr = ~$210.

steps: Be a registered voter in Colorado (15+ for student workers).
Submit the interest form on the official Jefferson County election-worker page.
Pass the background check and take the oath of office.
Attend all required trainings (paid) and work assigned shifts during the election period.
timing: Election-period temporary work; shifts vary by assignment and may include weekends.
